implementedFoundation: ResearchJob callback verification binds provider revision, HMAC signature, body hash, timestamp and nonce
the Research callback replay window is five minutes and nonce hashes are persisted with a tenant-scoped unique constraint
Research provider events bind provider execution id, sequence, event id, status and payload hash and detect gaps or replay drift
the callback transport intentionally does not trust a callback as final state and instructs the caller to pull provider state

findings.finding: there is no tenant-scoped canonical ActionWebhookInbox, ingress route or append-only webhook receipt linked to Action Attempt, provider request and account binding.

an external callback cannot safely choose org or project from caller headers; Action ingress needs endpoint credential or registration authority that resolves tenant, account and Adapter revision before payload parsing.

Action adapters expose execute and reconcile only; no versioned Adapter signature policy defines algorithm, canonical bytes, header mapping, key revision, timestamp window, rotation overlap or verification result.
there is no bounded raw-body quarantine with content hash, marking, malware and PII controls; parsing unverified or oversized webhook content would cross the trust boundary.
Research nonce persistence is reusable but not connected to Action provider identity or events; Action needs provider event id, nonce or body-hash replay keys and drift-conflict receipts.
no exact reducer binds a verified webhook event to one ActionExecutionAttempt, provider request id, actionBindingHash and Adapter schema; an unmatched event has no quarantine or investigation Case.
Action has no provider sequence, event time, received time, gap ledger, precedence rule or late-event policy, so out-of-order accepted, applied and failed events cannot be reduced safely.

verified webhook transport must append an Observation and trigger provider reread or deterministic reduction; it must never directly overwrite Proposal or Receipt status, but no Action reducer exists.

the legacy in-memory action_webhook helper stores bearer and basic credentials in auth_config and is mutable, non-tenant-scoped and non-authoritative; it cannot be reused as the W5 inbox or secret authority.

the reusable Research callback route still requires an AOS Principal; a provider-facing ingress needs a separately hardened authentication boundary without weakening tenant resolution or exposing canonical internal APIs.

verification.productionActionWebhookInboxScan: no canonical Action webhook inbox, ingress or reducer found
verification.legacyActionWebhookAssessment: mutable in-memory request-mapping helper only; not a W5 authority
verification.interpretation: Research callback security primitives are reusable, while the Action webhook authority and ordering semantics remain unimplemented
